items.title: Fred Lipsius interviewed by Monk Rowe. Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018
items.q: Coltrane and Sonny Rollins. Those were my favorite.

ctx.x: Are you actually thinking, okay, I’m on G minor 7 to C 7. Are you thinking that or are you not thinking that?

That’s a very good question and I’ve mentioned this a few times to some students, and usually they don’t ask me but I’ll tell them — first of all when I was younger, and I’m a pretty good improviser, better than most at 16, there was a certain point where I started to become good, listening, transcribing. I have a whole loose leaf book of solos so I developed my ear which was so-so I think, listening to Charlie Parker, Coltrane. Even one bar, write it down. You know, Cannonball, you know, Sonny Stitt — Bird,…

know the scene is coming up. Like if you’re in a boat and you’re going out to a destination, you know what you are seeing. You can see it, or imagine getting off the boat and walking in the sand and you reach the hotel or something. Whatever. I can kind of see that.
